speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I need to understand the cause of your acute diarrhea; how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent treatment with levofloxacin for pneumonia, your symptoms strongly suggest antibiotic-associated colitis. Have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool, or have you experienced fever or significant weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Antibiotic-Associated Colitis (Clostridioides difficile infection). The combination of recent levofloxacin use and acute watery diarrhea with cramping is highly characteristic of C. diff. Given the severity (9 episodes in 2 days), I am requesting a stool assay for C. difficile toxins immediately. REQUEST TEST: C_difficile_toxin_assay.
